cohort: Multigravida women (gravida 2 and above) with a pregnancy of more than 28 weeks gestation who had all previously delivered vaginally at least once at a gestation of more than 20 weeks, excluding those with prior abortions, prior cesarean sections, or pregnancies with medical conditions.
finding: Several factors, including malpresentation, fetal distress, antepartum hemorrhage, obstructed labor, severe preeclampsia/eclampsia, and twin pregnancy, contributed to primary cesarean sections in multigravida women, resulting in maternal and neonatal morbidity and mortality.
